coaching.summary: The graph is structurally sound and covers the three hard constraints well. The main gaps are missing links between team capacity and setup time, and no explicit weighting of the GDPR constraint as a hard knock-out criterion versus a scored factor.

strengthen_items.label: Connect team capacity to migration delay risk
strengthen_items.detail: A two-person team is itself a direct driver of setup time and therefore migration delay, but Data Team Capacity currently only flows to Data Team Capacity Strain — add an edge from Data Team Capacity to Migration and Setup Time to capture this dependency.

strengthen_items.label: Clarify EU residency as a hard constraint, not a scored factor
strengthen_items.detail: EU Data Residency Compliance is modelled symmetrically across all options, but the brief states it is eliminatory — make explicit that any option failing this factor is disqualified before scoring on cost or capability, so the goal node reflects a binary gate rather than a trade-off.

strengthen_items.label: Attach £120k ceiling to the budget factor
strengthen_items.detail: Annual Platform Cost has no numeric anchor in the graph, making Annual Budget Overrun Risk unverifiable — assign the £120k threshold explicitly so each option can be tested against a concrete pass/fail.

strengthen_items.label: Connect operational overhead to setup time
strengthen_items.detail: Higher ongoing operational overhead (e.g. self-hosted RudderStack or the Snowflake build) also lengthens initial migration and setup, so an edge from Operational Overhead on Data Team to Migration and Setup Time would capture this compounding effect on Migration Delay Before March Deadline.

elements_considered_but_excluded: vendor lock-in risk — relevant long-term but outside the March deadline scope
data volume / event throughput factor — important for cost modelling but not in the graph
negotiation leverage on current vendor — could affect status-quo cost but not modelled

bias_signals.detail: The March deadline is treated as fixed, but no buffer or contingency path is modelled if migration slips — Migration Delay Before March Deadline flows to the goal but there is no fallback option beyond Extend Current Contract (Status Quo).

Extend Current Contract (Status Quo) is included but may be implicitly underweighted if the team anchors on 'we must replace' — the graph should ensure it is evaluated on the same factor edges as the other options, which it is, but the brief language biases against it.

Vendor Ecosystem Maturity likely reflects familiarity with Segment (the most visible CDP brand) rather than an objective capability assessment, which could inflate perceived risk for Adopt RudderStack and Build on Snowflake with Fivetran.
